issues.legal_issue: A challenger cannot invalidate an acquisition notification on a fact-dependent eligibility ground without pleading the supporting facts.
material_facts: The challenge asserted that the persons for whose benefit the land was acquired were not refugees because they had not settled in the relevant state.
The writ petition did not plead that those persons were not settled there, and another ground in the petition assumed that they were refugees.
Whether the persons had settled there was a question of fact.
issues.conclusion: The challenge on this ground could not be sustained because the necessary factual averments had not been made.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(7) of the U.P. Land Acquisition (Rehabilitation of Refugees) Act, 1948 defined a refugee by reference to, among other things, migration to and continued residence in Uttar Pradesh. A party challenging a notification on a ground involving questions of fact must plead the necessary facts so that material bearing on the issue can be brought on record. No earlier case is relied on for this proposition in the judgment.

predicates.writ_challenge_to_acquisition_notificati: The challenger brought a writ proceeding seeking to invalidate an acquisition notification.
predicates.fact_dependent_eligibility_ground: The challenger relied on a claimed failure of beneficiary eligibility that depended on where the beneficiaries had lived or settled.
predicates.necessary_factual_averments: The challenger pleaded the facts needed to support the claimed eligibility failure.
predicates.factual_ground_not_sustained: The court does not sustain the challenge on that factual ground.

issues.definition: When a writ challenge to an acquisition notification rests on a fact-dependent eligibility ground, the ground is not sustained if the challenger did not plead the necessary facts.

issues.legal_issue: An acquisition notification can substantially comply with the law even if it omits a particular word, when its tenor shows that the government decided to acquire the land.
material_facts: The notification stated that the land was needed and suitable for the stated rehabilitation purpose.
It directed interested persons to appear for compensation determination and directed the collector to take possession.
It stated that the land would be deemed permanently acquired and vest absolutely in the state.
The notification did not use the word “decided.”
issues.conclusion: The notification substantially complied with the law because its tenor clearly showed the government's decision to acquire the land.
issues.legal_principle: Section 7(1) of the U.P. Land Acquisition (Rehabilitation of Refugees) Act, 1948 was applied. The court held that substantial compliance is sufficient and that an acquisition notification should not be struck down on hypertechnical grounds when its overall terms reveal the required decision. No earlier case is relied on for this proposition in the judgment.

predicates.acquisition_notification_challenge: The proceeding challenges the validity of a notification acquiring land.
predicates.notification_tenor_shows_acquisition_dec: The notification's recitals and operative terms, read as a whole, show that the government decided to acquire the land.
predicates.particular_decision_word_absent: The notification omits a particular word that would expressly state the government's decision.
predicates.notification_substantially_complies: The notification satisfies the applicable legal requirement through substantial compliance.

issues.definition: A challenged acquisition notification substantially complies when its overall terms show the acquisition decision, even though a particular word expressing that decision is absent.

issues.legal_issue: An acquisition notification is not vague when it refers to a site plan that identifies the land being acquired.
material_facts: The notification identified the relevant land by field numbers and area and expressly referred to a site plan available for inspection.
The fields' combined area exceeded the area being acquired, but evidence filed for the society stated that the acquired area was exactly one acre.
An official who later attempted to deliver possession had difficulty identifying the acquired portion, but he had not brought the correct plan.
issues.conclusion: The notification had not been shown to be vague, and the court found no sufficient ground to interfere with the finding that it properly identified the land.
issues.legal_principle: The court assessed the notification's identification of the land under section 7(1) of the U.P. Land Acquisition (Rehabilitation of Refugees) Act, 1948, including its express reference to the site plan and the evidence identifying the acquired area. No earlier case is relied on for this conclusion in the judgment.

predicates.acquisition_notification_challenge: The proceeding challenges the validity of a notification acquiring land.
predicates.notification_references_site_plan: The notification expressly refers to a site plan concerning the land to be acquired.
predicates.evidence_identifies_acquired_land: The available plan or other evidence identifies the land or area being acquired.
predicates.notification_not_shown_vague: The court does not find the notification vague on the basis of the challenge presented.

issues.definition: A challenged acquisition notification is not shown to be vague when it refers to a site plan and the evidence identifies the land being acquired.
